Read an openMSX replay

Source: R/readers.R
read_omr.Rd

Reads gzip-compressed openMSX XML replay files. Supported event schemas cover keyboard matrices, joysticks, mice, trackballs, paddles, touchpads, light guns, and autofire settings. The initial keyboard state is read from the first replay snapshot. Every device is one controller: the keyboard first, then the devices on the joystick ports by name, as listed in movie$header$controllers. Their controls have the same IDs as in every other reader: a joystick is the direction pad with A and B, the buttons of a mouse or trackball are A and B, the JoyMega pad adds C, Start, X, Y, Z and Mode, a light-gun trigger and a paddle's button are A, and a touch on the touchpad is L3. openmsx_key_r8_b0 identifies a keyboard matrix row and bit. All devices share one event stream, so each controller has a row for every event.

Usage

read_omr(
  path,
  analog = "raw",
  deadzone = NULL,
  triggers = "raw",
  aliases = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

path

Recording file path.

analog

Stick representation: "raw" (default), "cardinal4", "cardinal8", "angle", or "angle+magnitude". A scalar applies to both sticks; c(left = "cardinal8", right = "angle") selects them independently. Cardinal modes add separate left/right logical direction columns. Continuous modes return numeric fields through stick_channels(). Original X/Y values remain in analog_channels() in every mode. Absent sticks add no columns.

deadzone

Radial threshold in centred axis half-range units, from zero to one. One value applies to both sticks; named left/right values are allowed. NULL uses the default of the controller, whichever emulator recorded it: 0.125 for the sticks of Nintendo's consoles (Nintendo 64, GameCube, Wii extensions, 3DS) and 0.25 for all other sticks. The first is close to the 15 of 128 units that the GameCube's controller library discards on each axis (PAD_Clamp in libogc). The second covers the resting position of a released PlayStation stick, up to about 32 of 128 units from the centre (psx-spx), and is close to the 7849 and 8689 of 32767 that Microsoft gives for the thumbsticks of PC gamepads (XInput). A game applies a threshold of its own, which the recording does not store; give that value to study one game. Neutral observations have no direction and an NA angle. Magnitude is kept.

triggers

"raw" (default) or "digital". For DTM, digital additionally projects each analogue trigger at 128/255 into separate L2/R2 columns. Hardware L/R click bits remain distinct from thresholded analogue triggers.

aliases

TRUE (default) places the controls of a recording under the shared IDs that button_layout() describes. With FALSE, a control that would be placed under another control's ID keeps the key of its source, so every control of the recording has a column of its own and no two are combined.

...

Reader-specific arguments, such as controller_order for M64 or DTM, or member for a recording inside a ZIP archive (see movie_members()).

Value

A replayr_movie with event times, device controls, and source XML.

Details

Each row follows one replay event. movie$events$timestamp_ticks retains time in openMSX master-clock ticks (3,579,545 * 960 ticks per second), and timestamp_seconds expresses the same event times in seconds. timestamp_source, event_type, source_device, and source_xml retain the event's original time, type, device, and XML.

analog_channels() preserves the values of each device on its controller. Examples include mouse_dx and mouse_dy for movement and touch_x and touch_y for touch coordinates. A recorded autofire setting, such as openmsx_autofire_renshaturbo, belongs to the machine and is returned by system_channels(). Movement deltas apply to their event; coordinates and settings persist until updated. The replay schema version and machine name remain in movie$header$replay_version and movie$header$machine.

Examples

movie <- read_omr(system.file("extdata", "computers", "keyboard-joystick.omr", package = "replayr"))
# Every device is a controller.
movie$header$controllers
#> [1] "keyboard"     "keyjoystick1" "mouse"       
observation_time(movie)
#> [1] 0 1 1 2 2 2 3
